html:
Frédéric Chopin was a composer and pianist, born in 1810 in Żelazowa Wola near Warsaw to a French father and a Polish mother, whose works for solo piano are among the best loved in classical music.

A child prodigy in Warsaw, he left in 1830, weeks before the November Uprising, and never returned. In Paris he taught and played in salons rather than big halls. He wrote mazurkas and polonaises based on Polish dances, as well as nocturnes, études, ballades and two concertos. His long relationship with the novelist George Sand ended in 1847. He suffered from a lung illness for years and died in Paris at 39. His heart was taken to Warsaw and placed in a pillar of the Holy Cross Church. Warsaw's airport bears his name, and his music is a symbol of Poland.
